title: The normalizer Weyl group is the root reflection group
statement: Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Let $G$ be a reductive $F$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme], meaning smooth, connected, affine and of finite type with no nontrivial smooth connected normal unipotent subgroup. Fix a split maximal torus $T\subseteq G$ and a Borel subgroup $B\supseteq T$, with character lattice $X=X^*(T)$, roots $\Phi$, coroots $\alpha^\vee$ and perfect character-cocharacter pairing as in [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure]. Put $E=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbf Q}(\Phi)\subseteq X\otimes_{\mathbf Z}\mathbf Q$ and $W=N_G(T)(F)/T(F)$, acting on characters by $(w\chi)(t)=\chi(n_w^{-1}tn_w)$. Here the normalizer consists of those elements conjugating $T$ to itself. Then $W$ is finite, and restriction to $E$ is an injective homomorphism $W\to\operatorname{GL}_{\mathbf Q}(E)$ whose image is precisely the subgroup generated by the reflections $s_\alpha(x)=x-\langle x,\alpha^\vee\rangle\alpha$ for $\alpha\in\Phi$. The action permutes $\Phi$. In particular, this restriction identifies the normalizer quotient with the reflection group of the root system, including when $\Phi=\varnothing$ and both groups are trivial.

source.place: Theorem 21.37 and Corollary 21.38, printed pp.435--436; Appendix C.15, p.611, and C.46 with its proof, pp.618--619 (faithfulness on roots).

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-reductive-rank-one-reflections] to $(G,T)$. It gives finiteness of $W$ and its action on $X$ permuting $\Phi$. Explicitly, the character action is independent of a representative, since replacing $n$ by $nt_0$ inserts an inner conjugation by $t_0\in T(F)$ inside the commutative torus. The formula gives $(w_1w_2)\chi=w_1(w_2\chi)$ by substitution. Extend this lattice action rationally. Since $\Phi$ spans $E$ and is permuted, both $w$ and $w^{-1}$ preserve $E$. This defines the homomorphism $r:W\to\operatorname{GL}_{\mathbf Q}(E)$ in the statement.

source.place: Theorem 21.11(d)--(e), pp.428--430; Theorem 21.37, first sentences of proof, p.436.

proof.text: We first check that preserving $\Phi^+$ forces a representative to normalize $B$, without inferring equality of subgroups from equality of their Lie algebras. For $n\in N_G(T)(F)$ representing $w$ and $v\in\mathfrak g_\alpha$, one has $\operatorname{Ad}(t)\operatorname{Ad}(n)v=\operatorname{Ad}(n)\operatorname{Ad}(n^{-1}tn)v=(w\alpha)(t)\operatorname{Ad}(n)v$. Thus conjugation by $n$ carries $\mathfrak g_\alpha$ to $\mathfrak g_{w\alpha}$. The conjugate $nU_\alpha n^{-1}$ is smooth, connected, closed and $T$-normalized with this tangent space, hence equals $U_{w\alpha}$ by uniqueness in [lem-sfb-reductive-root-subgroup-parametrizations]. By [lem-sfb-borel-root-product-coordinates] and $B=R_u(B)\rtimes T$ from [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure], the subgroup $B$ is generated by $T$ and the $U_\alpha$ for $\alpha\in\Phi^+$. Indeed their ordered product followed by $T$ maps isomorphically onto $B$ as a scheme. If $w\Phi^+=\Phi^+$, conjugation by $n$ and its inverse preserve all these generating subgroups as a set. Therefore $nBn^{-1}=B$ as subgroup schemes.

source.place: 21.19, p.431; Theorem 21.68(a)--(b), p.445; explicit positive-root determination of the Borel in the chamber/Borel comparison of 21.37.

proof.text:
Suppose $w\Phi^+=\Phi^+$ and choose $n$ as above. The preceding step and [lem-sfb-borel-scheme-normalizer] give $n\in B(F)$. Let $p:B\to T$ be the homomorphism restricting to the identity on $T$ provided by [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure]. For every commutative $F$-algebra $A$ and $t\in T(A)$, normalizing $T$ and $p|_T=\mathrm{id}$ give
$$n_A t n_A^{-1}=p_A(n_A t n_A^{-1})=p_A(n_A)t p_A(n_A)^{-1}=t.$$
The last equality uses commutativity of $T$. The same equality holds after every algebra extension, so $n\in C_G(T)(F)$. By [lem-sfb-reductive-torus-self-centralizer], $n\in T(F)$ and $w=1$. We have proved that the stabilizer in $W$ of $\Phi^+$ is trivial. In particular $r(w)=1$ implies that $w$ fixes every root and preserves $\Phi^+$, so $w=1$; hence $r$ is injective.

source.place: Proposition 17.53, proof, p.369; Theorem 17.48, p.367; Proposition 17.61(a), p.372. The semidirect-product projection replaces the commutator calculation in 17.53.

proof.text:
Put $V=E\otimes_{\mathbf Q}\mathbf R$ and extend the finite $W$-action to $V$. The root datum and simple-root base in [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure] give a finite spanning root set and a basis $\Delta$, with integral coordinates of one sign for every root. Reducedness remains true over $\mathbf R$: proportional nonzero rational coordinate vectors have a rational proportionality factor. Choose any positive definite form $(\ ,\ )_0$ in this basis and set $(x,y)=\sum_{w\in W}(wx,wy)_0$. The identity summand makes this positive definite, and reindexing $w\mapsto wu$ proves $W$-invariance. By [lem-sfb-reductive-rank-one-reflections], each $s_\alpha\in W$ has formula $x\mapsto x-\langle x,\alpha^\vee\rangle\alpha$ and sends $\alpha$ to $-\alpha$. Invariance gives
$$(x,\alpha)-\langle x,\alpha^\vee\rangle(\alpha,\alpha)=(s_\alpha x,\alpha)=-(x,\alpha).$$
Thus $\langle x,\alpha^\vee\rangle=2(x,\alpha)/(\alpha,\alpha)$, so these are precisely the orthogonal root reflections. The coroots of [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure] give the same reflections on $E$: if $s'(x)=x-\langle x,\beta^\vee\rangle\alpha$ with $\langle\alpha,\beta^\vee\rangle=2$ also permutes $\Phi$, then $u=s_\alpha s'$ fixes $\alpha$, satisfies $u(x)-x\in\mathbf Q\alpha$ on $E$, and permutes the finite spanning set $\Phi$, so $u^m=1$ for some $m\geq1$. With $N=u-1$ one has $N^2=0$, hence $0=u^m-1=mN$ and $u=1$ on $E$. Their root pairings are integral by the integer character-cocharacter pairing, and they permute $\Phi$. All hypotheses of the real chamber theorem are now verified.

source.place: Appendix C.19--C.20, p.611; Theorem 21.37, p.436, passing from the root datum to its real root system.

proof.text: Let $W_\Phi\subseteq\operatorname{GL}_{\mathbf R}(V)$ be generated by these reflections. The preceding rank-one representatives show $W_\Phi\subseteq r_{\mathbf R}(W)$, where $r_{\mathbf R}$ denotes scalar extension of $r$. Fix $w\in W$. Its image sends the base $\Delta$ to the base $w\Delta$: linear independence and the integral coefficients of one sign are preserved. By $W$-invariance of the form, $wC_\Delta=C_{w\Delta}$. Apply [lem-sfb-root-chamber-simple-transitivity] to obtain $a\in W_\Phi$ with $aC_\Delta=C_{w\Delta}$. Write $a$ as a word in root reflections and take the same word in the rank-one elements of $W$, obtaining $h\in W$ with $r_{\mathbf R}(h)=a$. Then $h^{-1}w$ preserves $C_\Delta$. The chamber theorem identifies the positive roots with those having positive inner product with any point in this chamber; since $h^{-1}w$ is an isometry permuting roots, it therefore preserves $\Phi^+$. Step 3 gives $h^{-1}w=1$. Hence every $w$ is a word in the rank-one elements. Restricting their formulas to $E$ proves that $r(W)$ is exactly the group generated by the stated rational reflections. Equality after real scalar extension detects equality of rational linear maps, so this conclusion is over $\mathbf Q$.

source.place: Theorem 21.37 and Corollary 21.38, p.436; Appendix C.21--C.22, p.612. The trivial stabilizer was established directly in steps 2--3.

proof.text: If $\Phi=\varnothing$, then $E=0$ and every $w\in W$ preserves $\Phi^+=\varnothing$. Step 3 gives $W=\{1\}$. The group generated by the empty family of reflections on $E=0$ is also $\{1\}$. Thus the preceding identification includes the empty-root case.

source.place: Appendix C.15, p.611; the empty-root instance of the stabilizer argument above.

proof_origin.place: Theorem 21.37 and Corollary 21.38, p.436, with Proposition 17.53 and Appendix C.19--C.22; Borel determination expanded using 21.19 and 21.68(a)--(b).
